content.text:
Routing uses one root router plus six lazy-loaded feature routers. URLs use hashes because `HashLocationStrategy` is configured, e.g. `/#/t/123/u/4`.

## Overall structure

[app-routing.module.ts](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/app-routing.module.ts:24) calls `RouterModule.forRoot()` once. Feature modules call `RouterModule.forChild()`; their paths are appended to the lazy-load prefix.

| Effective path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/r/...` | Login and post-login landing flow |
| `/check/:workspace-id/:sys-check-name/...` | Syscheck |
| `/admin/:ws/...` | Workspace administration |
| `/superadmin/...` | Instance administration |
| `/gm/:group-name[/:profile-id]` | Group monitor |
| `/sm/:ws` | Study monitor |
| `/am/:group-name/...` | Attachment manager |
| `/t/...` | Test execution |
| `/legal-notice`, `/privacy`, `/accessibility` | Public information pages |

The router-outlet hierarchy is:

```text
AppComponent
└─ root <router-outlet>
   ├─ AppRootComponent for /r
   │  └─ child <router-outlet>
   └─ TestControllerComponent for /t/:t
      └─ child <router-outlet>
         ├─ TestStatusComponent
         └─ UnithostComponent
```

`AppRootComponent` is only a shell around an outlet. `TestControllerComponent` is a much more important shell: it loads the Test, handles commands, timers, persistence and navigation, while its child outlet switches between status UI and the current Unit.

## All `RouterModule` uses

Route definitions:

- [app-routing.module.ts](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/app-routing.module.ts:24): root routes and lazy-loading.
- [sys-check-routing.module.ts](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/sys-check/sys-check-routing.module.ts:22): defaults to welcome, then network check, questionnaire, report or Unit check.
- [workspace-routing.module.ts](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/workspace-admin/workspace-routing.module.ts:10): files, syscheck, results and tests.
- [superadmin-routing.module.ts](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/superadmin/superadmin-routing.module.ts:8): users, workspaces and settings.
- [group-monitor-routing.module.ts](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/group-monitor/group-monitor-routing.module.ts:5): group monitor with optional profile.
- [study-monitor-routing.module.ts](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/study-monitor/routing/study-monitor-routing.module.ts:5): study monitor.
- [attachment-manager-routing.module.ts](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/attachment-manager/routing/attachment-manager-routing.module.ts:7): overview and image capture.
- [test-controller-routing.module.ts](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/test-controller/routing/test-controller-routing.module.ts:11): Test status and Unit execution.

The plain `RouterModule` imports in `AppModule` and `SysCheckModule` do not add routes. They expose directives such as `routerLink`, `routerLinkActive`, and `router-outlet`. They appear partly redundant because the routing modules already export `RouterModule`; likely legacy explicit imports.

One suspicious unrelated legacy detail: `/admin/:ws` redirects to `monitor`, but no `monitor` child exists. Its `**` route then displays `FilesComponent` while leaving `monitor` in the URL.

## Why `route-dispatcher` exists

The name is misleading. The component does not dispatch anything. [RouteDispatcherComponent](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/app-root/route-dispatcher/route-dispatcher.component.ts:12) only displays “page not found”.

The actual dispatcher is [RouteDispatcherActivateGuard](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/app-route-guards.ts:14). It examines stored authentication data and sends the Login to:

- `/r/login` when unauthenticated
- `/r/code-input` when an entry code is required
- directly into their sole Test or Syscheck after direct login
- `/r/starter` otherwise

Thus `/r/route-dispatcher` is a stable decision point. Other code can navigate to `/r` without duplicating the “where should this Login go?” logic.

Git history confirms this was introduced in 2020 as a central token-based landing mechanism. The component was also reused as the 404 page, causing the confusing name and dual responsibility.

## Why `path: ''` goes there

There are two empty redirects:

```text
/   → /r/route-dispatcher
/r  → /r/route-dispatcher
```

Both use `pathMatch: 'full'`, so they match only the exact empty path at their respective level.

That provides equivalent behavior for:

- opening the application root
- code navigating to `/r`
- the direct-login guard finishing authentication and returning `/r`

The dispatcher guard then chooses the real destination. Under normal operation, `RouteDispatcherComponent` is never rendered for this route because its guard always returns a redirect.

## Difference between `''` and `**`

They are opposites:

- `''` means “no remaining path segment”.
- `**` means “any remaining path that no earlier route matched”.

Route order matters: Angular chooses the first matching route, so `**` must be last.

They also do not really lead to the dispatcher in the same way:

```text
Exact /
  → redirect /r/route-dispatcher
  → RouteDispatcherActivateGuard
  → login, starter, code input, Test or Syscheck

Unknown /alice
  → ** route
  → DirectLoginActivateGuard treats "alice" as a Login name
  → authenticate
  → /r
  → normal dispatcher flow

Unknown /something/else
  → ** route
  → direct-login guard permits activation
  → RouteDispatcherComponent displays 404
```

See [DirectLoginActivateGuard](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/app-route-guards.ts:68).

Consequently, every unknown single-segment path is interpreted as a direct-login name. That is a legacy URL feature, not ordinary 404 behavior.

## Why `TestStatusComponent` exists

It is the Test’s non-Unit screen. [Its template](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/test-controller/components/test-status/test-status.component.html:1) handles several states:

- loading
- paused
- error
- termination in progress
- active Test with resume/end actions

This separation lets `TestControllerComponent` remain mounted and keep the Test, command subscriptions, timers and loaded Booklet alive while its child outlet replaces `UnithostComponent` with status UI.

Pause and error navigation explicitly goes to status in [test-controller.service.ts](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/test-controller/services/test-controller.service.ts:551). It usually uses `skipLocationChange`, suggesting status was designed as an internal state screen rather than a meaningful bookmarkable URL.

## The three apparent status routes

They are actually:

```text
/t/:t
  → redirects its empty child to status
  → /t/:t/status

/t/:t/status
  → TestControllerComponent shell
  → TestStatusComponent in its child outlet

/t/status
  → TestStatusComponent directly, without TestControllerComponent
```

Therefore `''` is not another global status route. It is the empty child beneath `:t`. Opening `/t/123` redirects to `/t/123/status`.

`/t/status` is the odd one. It was added in March 2024 to fix issue #459. Previously, because `:t` accepts any string, `/t/status` was interpreted as:

```text
t = 'status'
```

`TestControllerComponent` would then try loading a Test whose ID was literally `status`, contributing to a repeated-error/navigation loop. The explicit `status` route is placed before `:t`, so it wins first-match routing and prevents that.

Its comment—“under some circumstances we get to the status page without having a test-Id”—is essentially an admission that this is a defensive legacy workaround. It is not a clean second form of the normal Test route. The coherent route is `/t/:t/status`; `/t/status` exists to safely render error/status UI when initialization has already lost the Test ID.
should RouteDispatcherComponent be renamed then? only leaving the guard actually being the real dispatcher

Yes. Rename `RouteDispatcherComponent` to `NotFoundComponent` or `PageNotFoundComponent`.

Keep:

- `RouteDispatcherActivateGuard`: actual dispatcher.
- `route-dispatcher` path: internal landing/decision endpoint.
- `NotFoundComponent`: attached both as the guarded endpoint’s unreachable fallback and the `**` 404 view.

This clarifies the existing behavior without changing routing. Renaming the path would be riskier because `/r/route-dispatcher` is referenced explicitly by Test deactivation logic.

Longer term, the cleaner design would separate the dispatcher endpoint completely from the wildcard:

```ts
{ path: 'route-dispatcher', component: EmptyComponent, canActivate: [RouteDispatcherActivateGuard] }
{ path: '**', component: NotFoundComponent, canActivate: [DirectLoginActivateGuard] }
```

But that extra component adds little value. The minimal component-only rename is worthwhile.

content.text:
A dialog can render the same UI, but replacing the status route with a dialog is not safe as a simple refactor.

The route currently provides lifecycle behavior:

- Leaving `u/:u` destroys `UnithostComponent` and its Verona Player iframe.
- `UnitDeactivateGuard` runs persistence and leave-restriction checks.
- Paused/error state prevents Unit activation through `TestControllerErrorPausedActivateGuard`.
- `/t/:t/status` keeps `TestControllerComponent` alive while removing the Unit.
- `/t/status` remains the defensive no-Test-ID error route.
- Resume navigation automatically destroys `TestStatusComponent`.

A dialog opened over the current Unit would leave the iframe, subscriptions and possibly Player activity running underneath. The modal blocks normal clicks, but it does not deactivate the route or destroy the Player.

The current [MessageService](/home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/frontend/src/app/shared/services/message.service.ts:24) functions are also insufficient:

- dialogs are dismissible through backdrop/Escape;
- the info dialog has a close button;
- the info title is hard-coded to `Anleitung`, ignoring `data.title`;
- confirm dialogs only support two fixed closing actions;
- nothing automatically closes a status dialog when remote commands resume the Test.

Recommended approach: keep the status routes, but make the routed `TestStatusComponent` open a dedicated status dialog.

```text
Unit route
  → pause/error navigation
  → Unit guard and teardown
  → status route activates
  → TestStatusComponent opens dialog
  → resume navigates to Unit
  → status component destroyed
  → dialog explicitly closed
```

The dedicated dialog should use `disableClose: true`, support the state-specific actions, and be closed in `TestStatusComponent.ngOnDestroy()`. This gives you dialog presentation while preserving routing semantics.

I would not use `showInfoDialog()` or `showConfirmDialog()` for this. Add a dedicated `showTestStatusDialog()` or open a dedicated `TestStatusDialogComponent` through `MatDialog`.

Removing the status routes entirely is possible, but then you must explicitly reproduce Unit teardown, buffer flushing, route guards, non-dismissible behavior, remote pause/resume handling, reload recovery, and `/t/status` error fallback. That would be a substantial state-machine redesign, not merely a UI change.
does calling the statuscomponent also lead to destruction of testcontrollercomponent?

No—normally it preserves `TestControllerComponent`.

For `/t/:t/status`, the route hierarchy is:

```text
TestControllerComponent        /t/:t
└─ TestStatusComponent         status
```

Navigating between:

```text
/t/123/u/4
/t/123/status
```

only replaces the component inside `TestControllerComponent`’s `<router-outlet>`:

- `UnithostComponent` is destroyed.
- `TestStatusComponent` is created.
- `TestControllerComponent` remains alive.
- Its Test data, subscriptions, command handling and services remain available.

`TestControllerComponent` is destroyed only when leaving `/t/:t` entirely, changing to a different Test ID, or otherwise causing Angular not to reuse that parent route.

Exception: `/t/status` is a separate top-level child route of `/t`. It renders `TestStatusComponent` without a `TestControllerComponent` parent. Navigating from `/t/123/...` to `/t/status` therefore destroys `TestControllerComponent`. That route is only a defensive error workaround, not the normal status flow.

content.text:
Yes—you are one commit off: `f55886b` is the release commit and parent of `d10be12c7`, which added `/status`.

The actual loop was:

```text
An error occurs before TestControllerComponent starts
→ ReplaySubject stores it
→ TestControllerComponent subscribes before reading route parameter :t
→ stored error immediately calls errorOut()
→ tcs.testId is still ''
→ navigation becomes /t/status
→ :t interprets "status" as a Test ID
→ another TestControllerComponent starts
→ same stored error replays
→ loop
```

`d10be12c7` addressed this in two ways:

- clears the buffered error before subscribing;
- adds literal `/t/status` before `/:t`, preventing `status` from becoming a Test ID.

Using `TestStatusComponent` there was a pragmatic shortcut: `errorOut()` already sets state to `ERROR`, and `TestStatusComponent` already renders `ErrorComponent`. But conceptually it is confusing and unsafe. If someone manually visits `/t/status` while the state is not `ERROR`, it may show resume/end actions despite having no Test ID.

I would separate the routes:

```ts
{
  path: 'error',
  component: TestInitializationErrorComponent
},
{
  path: ':t',
  component: TestControllerComponent,
  children: [
    { path: '', redirectTo: 'status', pathMatch: 'full' },
    { path: 'status', component: TestStatusComponent },
    { path: 'u/:u', component: UnithostComponent }
  ]
}
```

Then make error navigation explicit:

```ts
if (this.testId) {
  return this.router.navigate(['/t', this.testId, 'status']);
}

return this.router.navigate(['/t/error']);
```

`TestInitializationErrorComponent` should only:

- render the captured error;
- offer reload/logout according to error type;
- optionally return to `/r/starter` after explicitly resetting Test state.

It should not silently redirect immediately: that would hide the error and may retry with stale state.

The deeper fix belongs in error ownership, not routing. `TestControllerComponent` should establish `testId` before subscribing to errors, and stale errors should be acknowledged when leaving the error flow or starting a genuinely new Test. Calling `clearErrorBuffer()` immediately before subscription is fragile because it can discard a legitimate initialization error.

So my recommendation:

1. Keep `/t/:t/status` for normal Test states.
2. Replace top-level `/t/status` with a dedicated initialization-error route/component.
3. Initialize `testId` before subscribing to `appError$`.
4. Treat buffer clearing as explicit error acknowledgement, not loop prevention.
